It measured no step cost. - The GDN check calls the private `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend`, as `olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py` already does. ### Alternatives considered | option | why not | |---|---| | rules inside `Scheduler` | about 50 lines in 6 core files, plus a one-model `SchedulerConfig` field | | prefix caching off | no core change, but loses the 1.58x / 1.51x DI speed-up | | content keys in block hashes | correct for connectors and offloading by construction, but needs `request.py` / `kv_cache_utils.py` changes and chunked prefill off server-wide | | a new hook on `DefaultModelState` that the model state overrides | extends the core model-state interface for one model | | writing the ranges onto the built `TritonAttentionMetadata` | the same reads and 35 fewer source lines, but the model state would edit objects the base class built, and a composite backend would never see the ranges | | `TRITON_FLASHINFER` (routes PrefixLM steps to Triton, decode to FlashInfer) | the ranges reach it through `mm_req_doc_ranges`, and it gives the same answers on B200, but it measured no gain (earlier head: decisions/s at c64 0.8% lower, the same decode tok/s), so the hook refuses it | ### Related work #63033 (open, fixes #62968) makes PaliGemma's whole prompt one bidirectional block. It adds a flag in `Scheduler` and turns chunked prefill and prefix caching off. This PR serves another model family, with two request-defined blocks, keeps prefix caching and leaves `scheduler.py` and the core model states alone. ### Limitations - `TRITON_ATTN` and Model Runner V2 only. - `Qwen3_5ForSlotDecision` subclasses `model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py` and runs with torch.compile, like the other Qwen3.5 derivatives on main (D3, colqwen3_5, minicpmv4_6). Hi @simon-veitner-redhat, thanks for the PrefixLM scheduler. We use it to cache the state blocks of Decision 3.0
`prefix_bidir` requests (vllm-sr/d3-turbo, a Qwen3.5 GDN hybrid). On the way we found a few things in this PR's
code that you may want:

1. **Requests with media keep their prefix.** `prefix_lm_len` was dropped for every request with media, so the
   prompt was read causally and never cached. The prefix is now kept unless a media item runs across its end
   (streamed requests still drop it), and each media item inside the prefix goes into the prefix salt.
2. **Warn when prefixes can barely be cached.** With a Mamba backend that saves no prefill checkpoints (e.g. the
   Triton/FLA GDN backend on main), a prefix is reused only when its length is a multiple of the Mamba block size.
   The scheduler now says so once.
3. **A PrefixLM prompt no step can prefill.** It returned 0 tokens forever, a silent head-of-line hang. It now
   finishes with a validation error. Only the prompt has to fit a step; outputs of a resumed request don't count.

(We also had to set `supports_mm_inputs` in the hybrid model state tests. Your later commit does the same, so
ignore that one.)

Links: https://github.com/zamog/vllm/commit/5bfa937c8bcd1713958e55385ebca3c98cc127d2, https://github.com/zamog/vllm/commit/3e6fd3d9d24ae0c9ea9aad683f509bacdc6e15cb, https://github.com/zamog/vllm/commit/4e9422292bb6711c354c6ee3f6c8a39ab9df73d5 (refined in https://github.com/zamog/vllm/commit/f9584f12146ceda6c1e2d69a83877faacb89eac7)

What D3 needs on top, proposed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64267:
- a per-request prefix-cache hit cap, which the scheduler sets for PrefixLM requests and KV connectors honour;
- Mamba checkpoints at the cap, with a prefix match unit finer than the block;
- no cache writes from a prompt resumed inside a block;
- CPU offload of states saved inside a block.

How would you like this stacked? We can send 1–3 as commits for your branch, or as a follow-up PR after yours
merges.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write these changes, and AI agents reviewed them. Not all of the code has

I'd like to keep this PR to the two models it serves and take your three fixes as a follow-up PR once this one merges. Here is how each one meets the current branch:

Keeping the prefix needs the same rule in both places, plus the media hashes in the prefix salt as you did.
2. **Warning when the cache is nearly useless.** The slot model's config hook turns prefix caching off unless the GDN prefill backend is FlashInfer, so mammoth-1 and elephant-1 never reach this case. The warning matters for other models that pick `PrefixLMScheduler`, so it belongs in the scheduler.

Otherwise `num_new_tokens = 0` keeps the request at the queue head. A whole prompt from a block boundary skips the Mamba split. | `_mamba_block_aligned_split` | | Hits need the same prefix: a missing or forged salt is moved into its own namespace, and causal requests are moved out of it | `add_request` | | Streamed and multimodal requests are read causally (one-time warning), with or without prefix caching | `add_request` | | A step that ends inside a block raises instead of returning a wrong read | model state | | FULL CUDA graphs run one-token queries, so the model state skips the ranges there | model state | Requests without `prefix_lm_len` are scheduled exactly as by `Scheduler`. Under async scheduling, `PrefixLMScheduler.__new__` builds `PrefixLMAsyncScheduler`, because the model hook picks the scheduler before async scheduling is decided. ### Defaults the model sets | setting | value | |---|---| | `--max-model-len` | 16,384, the trained length, when not set (`max_position_embeddings` is 262,144). An explicit value is kept. | | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | raised to `--max-model-len` when below it, as `EngineArgs` does with chunked prefill off | | attention backend | `TRITON_ATTN` (the only one that applies the ranges per request) | | prefix caching | on with FlashInfer GDN prefill (Hopper, or Blackwell with CUDA 13). Otherwise turned off with a log line. | | scheduler | `PrefixLMScheduler`, with chunked prefill on with prefix caching and off without it | ### Refusals At startup: - KV connectors, `--kv-offloading-size`, speculative decoding, context parallelism and micro-batching - any attention backend other than `TRITON_ATTN` for full attention, including through `backend_per_kind` - `--max-num-scheduled-tokens` below `--max-model-len` - `--scheduler-cls`, and with prefix caching `--prefix-match-unit` - Model Runner V1 - unknown `modeling_overrides`, or `n_slots` outside 1-256 Per request (400): `instructions`, `chat_template_kwargs` other than `{"enable_thinking": false}`, media, prompts that do not fit `--max-model-len` with the answer token, scores with more than 10 levels, and `/v1/decisions` options with repeated labels. If `SlotLMStrategy` cannot start (for example on a non-fp32 head), a warning says why `/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` are off. ### Trade-offs - The step budget is only raised to `--max-model-len`. While decodes run, a full-length slot prompt waits at the queue head until they leave room: a 32,514-token read behind 256 decodes waited 13.35 s at a 32,768 budget and 1.07 s at 33,792 (earlier head). Set `--max-num-batched-tokens` to `--max-model-len` plus `--max-num-seqs` to avoid the wait. - `PrefixLMScheduler` overrides two private `Scheduler` methods. If upstream renames them, the behaviour tests fail and the model-state guard raises instead of returning wrong reads. - `PrefixLMScheduler` needs Mamba `align` mode, so a non-hybrid PrefixLM model cannot reuse it as is. - `cache_salt` changes meaning on this server. KV-event consumers see `prefix-lm:[:]`. - `MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS` 128 → 256 (Python and Rust) doubles `LogprobTokenIdsState` on every MRV2 server: 1 MiB at 1,024 requests. It measured no step cost. - The GDN check calls the private `_resolve_gdn_prefill_backend`, as `olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py` already does. ### Alternatives considered | option | why not | |---|---| | rules inside `Scheduler` | about 50 lines in 6 core files, plus a one-model `SchedulerConfig` field | | prefix caching off | no core change, but loses the 1.58x / 1.51x DI speed-up | | content keys in block hashes | correct for connectors and offloading by construction, but needs `request.py` / `kv_cache_utils.py` changes and chunked prefill off server-wide | | a new hook on `DefaultModelState` that the model state overrides | extends the core model-state interface for one model | | writing the ranges onto the built `TritonAttentionMetadata` | the same reads and 35 fewer source lines, but the model state would edit objects the base class built, and a composite backend would never see the ranges | | `TRITON_FLASHINFER` (routes PrefixLM steps to Triton, decode to FlashInfer) | the ranges reach it through `mm_req_doc_ranges`, and it gives the same answers on B200, but it measured no gain (earlier head: decisions/s at c64 0.8% lower, the same decode tok/s), so the hook refuses it | ### Related work #63033 (open, fixes #62968) makes PaliGemma's whole prompt one bidirectional block. It adds a flag in `Scheduler` and turns chunked prefill and prefix caching off. This PR serves another model family, with two request-defined blocks, keeps prefix caching and leaves `scheduler.py` and the core model states alone. ### Limitations - `TRITON_ATTN` and Model Runner V2 only. - `Qwen3_5ForSlotDecision` subclasses `model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py` and runs with torch.compile, like the other Qwen3.5 derivatives on main (D3, colqwen3_5, minicpmv4_6). It does not use main's new eager Qwen3.5 model. - `/v1/decisions` reads every question as a choice, so a predicate is rendered as a two-option choice rather than the trained yes/no prompt. - An explicit large `--max-model-len` is kept. +### Mammoth-1 and Elephant-1
+
+Base Labs [`baselabs/mammoth-1`](https://huggingface.co/baselabs/mammoth-1)

+```bash
+vllm serve baselabs/mammoth-1
+```
+
+- The full attention layers read the shared prefix and the question as two
+  bidirectional blocks, and each prompt is prefilled in one step, so a
+  `--max-num-batched-tokens` below `--max-model-len` is raised to it.
+  `--max-model-len` defaults to the trained 16,384 tokens.
+- Prefix caching (on by default) prefills the shared prefix once per decision
+  request instead of once per question. It needs FlashInfer's GatedDeltaNet
+  prefill (Hopper, or Blackwell with CUDA 13) and is turned off with other
+  backends.
+- A `choice` can have up to 255 options, labeled `A` to `Z` and then with
+  two-letter labels in the prompt. Media inputs return 400.
+- Only Model Runner V2 and the `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend are supported,
+  and the backend is selected automatically. KV transfer connectors,
+  `--kv-offloading-size`, speculative decoding, context parallelism,
+  micro-batching, `--prefix-match-unit` and `--scheduler-cls` are refused.
+- `instructions` returns 400, as does any `chat_template_kwargs` other than
+  `{"enable_thinking": false}`. `/v1/decisions` reads every question as a
+  choice and returns 400 for score levels with the same label.

+MODEL_NAME = "tiny-slot-decision"

+STATE = {
+    "ticket": "My card was charged twice for the same order. " * 20,
+    "customer": {"tenure_months": 14, "vip": False},
+}
+QUESTIONS = {
+    "refund": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the customer asking for money?"},
+    "team": {
+        "type": "choice",
+        "instructions": "Which team should handle this?",
+        "criteria": {"billing": "charges", "technical": "bugs", "sales": "pricing"},
+    },
+    "mood": {
+        "type": "score",
+        "instructions": "How frustrated is the customer?",
+        "criteria": ["calm", "irritated", "angry"],
+    },
+}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def server(tmp_path_factory):
+    checkpoint = str(tmp_path_factory.mktemp("slot-decision"))
+    build_tiny_checkpoint(checkpoint)
+    args = [
+        "--dtype",
+        "bfloat16",
+        "--served-model-name",
+        MODEL_NAME,
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "2048",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "8",
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.3",
+        "--limit-mm-per-prompt",
+        json.dumps({"image": 0, "video": 0}),
+    ]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(checkpoint, args) as remote_server:
+        yield remote_server
+
+
+def systemone(server, **body):
+    return requests.post(
+        server.url_for("v1/systemone"),
+        json={"model": MODEL_NAME, "state": STATE, "questions": QUESTIONS, **body},
+    )
+
+
+def check_probabilities(probabilities: dict[str, float], names: set[str]) -> None:
+    assert set(probabilities) == names
+    assert all(0.0 <= p <= 1.0 for p in probabilities.values())
+    assert sum(probabilities.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-4)
+
+
+def test_systemone(server):
+    response = systemone(server)
+    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+    body = response.json()
+    assert body["object"] == "structured_decision"
+    answers = body["answers"]
+    assert list(answers) == list(QUESTIONS)
+
+    # The answers themselves are built by the question types, tested on CPU.
+    check_probabilities(answers["refund"]["probabilities"], {"yes", "no"})
+    check_probabilities(
+        answers["team"]["probabilities"], {"billing", "technical", "sales"}
+    )
+    check_probabilities(answers["mood"]["probabilities"], {"0", "1", "2"})
+    for qid in answers:
+        assert 0.0 < body["diagnostics"][qid]["label_mass"] <= 1.0 + 1e-6
+    # One sampled token per question.
+    assert body["usage"]["output_tokens"] == len(QUESTIONS)
+
+    # The repeat reads the state from the prefix cache.
+    again = systemone(server)
+    assert again.status_code == 200, again.text
+    for qid, answer in again.json()["answers"].items():
+        assert answer["probabilities"] == pytest.approx(

+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "extra,match",
+    [
+        ({"images": ["data:image/png;base64,AAAA"]}, "does not take image inputs"),
+        ({"instructions": "Be strict."}, "takes no instructions"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_systemone_refusals(server, extra, match):
+    response = systemone(server, **extra)
+    assert response.status_code == 400
+    assert match in response.json()["error"]["message"]
+
+
+def test_decisions(server):
+    response = requests.post(
+        server.url_for("v1/decisions"),
+        json={
+            "model": MODEL_NAME,
+            "input": "The package arrived with a broken screen.",
+            "questions": [
+                {"type": "predicate", "instructions": "Is the screen broken?"},
+                {
+                    "type": "choice",
+                    "instructions": "Which department should handle this?",
+                    "choices": [{"value": "returns"}, {"value": "billing"}],
+                },
+            ],
+        },
+    )

+    assert 0.0 <= predicate["probability"] <= 1.0
+    probabilities = {p["value"]: p["probability"] for p in choice["probabilities"]}
+    check_probabilities(probabilities, {"returns", "billing"})

+"""Qwen3_5ForSlotDecision's block attention against the transformers block mask,
+on a random four-layer model built from BLOCK_ATTN_BASE."""

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.models.test_qwen3_5_slot import OVERRIDES
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+BASE = os.environ.get("BLOCK_ATTN_BASE", "baselabs/elephant-1")
+NUM_SCORED = 256
+# bf16 vLLM against an fp32 reference.
+ATOL = 0.1
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.hybrid_model,
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="block attention needs a CUDA GPU"
+    ),
+]

+def build_tiny_checkpoint(path: str) -> None:
+    from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoProcessor, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
+
+    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(BASE)
+    config.text_config.update({
+        "hidden_size": 256, "intermediate_size": 512, "num_hidden_layers": 4,
+        "layer_types": ["linear_attention", "full_attention"] * 2,
+        "num_attention_heads": 4, "num_key_value_heads": 2,
+        "linear_num_key_heads": 2, "linear_num_value_heads": 2,
+        "mtp_num_hidden_layers": 0, "dtype": "float32",
+    })  # fmt: skip
+    config.vision_config.update({
+        "depth": 1, "hidden_size": 64, "num_heads": 2, "intermediate_size": 128,
+        "out_hidden_size": 256,
+    })  # fmt: skip
+    config.modeling_overrides = OVERRIDES
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    model = Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration(config).to(torch.float32)
+    # Sharper weights and stronger attention values/outputs make the mask move
+    # the last token's logits well above bf16 noise.
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
+            if param.dim() > 1:
+                strong = "self_attn.v_proj" in name or "self_attn.o_proj" in name
+                param.normal_(0.0, 0.32 if strong else 0.08)
+    model.save_pretrained(path)
+    AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(BASE).save_pretrained(path)
+
+
+def hf_logprobs(path: str, prompts: dict, prefix_len: int) -> list[dict]:
+    """Last-position logprobs over the first NUM_SCORED tokens of each prompt,
+    with the prefix and the rest as two blocks, then causal."""
+    from transformers import Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration
+    from transformers.models.qwen3_5 import modeling_qwen3_5 as hf
+
+    model = Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
+        path, dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="sdpa"
+    ).to("cuda")
+    mask = hf.create_causal_mask
+
+    def run(prompt: list[int], blocked: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+        ids = (torch.arange(len(prompt), device="cuda") >= prefix_len).long()[None]
+        patched = partial(mask, block_sequence_ids=ids if blocked else None)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(hf, "create_causal_mask", patched)
+        with torch.inference_mode():
+            logits = model(input_ids=torch.tensor([prompt], device="cuda")).logits
+        return torch.log_softmax(logits[0, -1].float(), -1)[:NUM_SCORED].cpu()
+
+    with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as monkeypatch:
+        return [{q: run(p, b) for q, p in prompts.items()} for b in (True, False)]
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enforce_eager", [True, False])
+def test_block_attention_matches_transformers(vllm_runner, tmp_path, enforce_eager):
+    from vllm import SamplingParams
+    from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt
+
+    checkpoint = str(tmp_path)
+    build_tiny_checkpoint(checkpoint)
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1)
+
+    def tokens(n: int) -> list[int]:
+        return torch.randint(1000, 100000, (n,), generator=g).tolist()
+
+    # A long shared prefix, then three questions.
+    prefix = tokens(700)
+    shared = tokens(40)
+    questions = {
+        "q0": prefix + tokens(90),
+        "q1": prefix + shared + tokens(50),
+        "q2": prefix + shared + tokens(50),
+    }
+    p = len(prefix)
+    expected, causal = hf_logprobs(checkpoint, questions, p)
+    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+    for q in questions:
+        # The mask must matter, or the comparison proves nothing.
+        assert (causal[q] - expected[q]).abs().max() > 5 * ATOL, q
+
+    def params(prefix_len: int | None) -> SamplingParams:
+        return SamplingParams(
+            max_tokens=1,
+            temperature=0.0,
+            logprob_token_ids=list(range(NUM_SCORED)),
+            extra_args=None if prefix_len is None else {"prefix_lm_len": prefix_len},
+        )
+
+    # Room for every prompt in one step, so the reads share a batch.
+    with vllm_runner(
+        checkpoint,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        max_model_len=2048,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=4096,
+        enable_prefix_caching=True,
+        enforce_eager=enforce_eager,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.4,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 0},
+    ) as runner:
+        llm = runner.llm
+        vllm_config = llm.llm_engine.vllm_config
+        assert vllm_config.model_config.head_dtype == torch.float32
+        # Prefix caching stays on with FlashInfer's GDN prefill only.
+        prefix_caching = vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
+        if prefix_caching:
+            scheduler_cls = vllm_config.scheduler_config.scheduler_cls
+            assert scheduler_cls.startswith("vllm.v1.core.sched.prefix_lm_scheduler.")
+
+        # The three questions with their blocks, then q0 without a prefix length,
+        # which is read causally.
+        outputs = llm.generate(
+            [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=questions[q]) for q in [*questions, "q0"]],
+            [params(p)] * len(questions) + [params(None)],
+            use_tqdm=False,
+        )
+        references = [*expected.values(), causal["q0"]]
+
+        def check(name: str, out, reference) -> None:
+            logprobs = out.outputs[0].logprobs[0]
+            got = torch.tensor([logprobs[t].logprob for t in range(NUM_SCORED)])
+            error = (got - reference).abs().max().item()
+            assert error < ATOL, (name, error)
+
+        for args in zip([*questions, "q0 causal"], outputs, references):
+            check(*args)
+
+        if not prefix_caching:
+            return
+        # The prefix alone, as the strategy's warm-up sends it. The questions
+        # then reuse its cache, and never past it: q1 and q2 share 40 more
+        # tokens, and q2 comes twice.
+        llm.generate(TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=prefix), params(p), use_tqdm=False)
+        for name in ("q1", "q2", "q2"):
+            (out,) = llm.generate(
+                TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=questions[name]),
+                params(p),
+                use_tqdm=False,
+            )
+            check(f"{name} cached", out, expected[name])
+            assert 0 < (out.num_cached_tokens or 0) <= p, out.num_cached_tokens

+def make_scheduler(budget: int = 256, cls: type[Scheduler] = PrefixLMScheduler):
+    return create_scheduler(

+def make_request(req_id, prompt, prefix_len, salt="own", resumable=False):
+    """A PrefixLM request with the strategy's salt, or causal if prefix_len is None."""
+    if salt == "own":
+        salt = None if prefix_len is None else prefix_lm_salt(prompt[:prefix_len], None)
+    extra_args = None if prefix_len is None else {PREFIX_LM_LEN: prefix_len}
+    params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, extra_args=extra_args)
+    params.update_from_generation_config({}, EOS_TOKEN_ID)
+    init_none_hash(sha256)
+    return Request(
+        request_id=req_id,
+        prompt_token_ids=prompt,
+        sampling_params=params,
+        pooling_params=None,
+        cache_salt=salt,
+        resumable=resumable,
+        block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(16, sha256),
+    )
+
+
+def step(scheduler: Scheduler, *requests: Request) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
+    """Add the requests and run one step. Returns the cached and scheduled
+    tokens of each new request."""
+    for request in requests:
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    ids = list(output.num_scheduled_tokens)
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        output,
+        ModelRunnerOutput(ids, {i: n for n, i in enumerate(ids)}, [[0]] * len(ids)),
+    )
+    return {
+        r.req_id: (r.num_computed_tokens, output.num_scheduled_tokens[r.req_id])
+        for r in output.scheduled_new_reqs
+    }

+"""The fixed prompt of slot-readout decision models, byte for byte as trained."""
+
+import json
+from typing import Any
+
+from .question_types import LABELS
+
+SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
+    "Apply the question to the state. Choose exactly one of the listed options. "
+    "Respond with only its uppercase letter, with no explanation or reasoning."
+)
+#: Two-letter labels that are not one token in the Qwen3.5 vocabulary.
+_NOT_ONE_TOKEN = frozenset({
+    "BQ", "BZ", "CJ", "CQ", "CZ", "DQ", "DZ", "EJ", "EY", "FJ", "FQ", "FV", "FZ",
+    "GJ", "GK", "GQ", "GZ", "HJ", "IY", "JF", "JG", "JH", "JL", "JN", "JQ",
+})  # fmt: skip
+_PAIRS = tuple(a + b for a in LABELS for b in LABELS if a + b not in _NOT_ONE_TOKEN)
+#: Slot i labels option i: A to Z, then the two-letter labels in order.
+SLOT_LABELS = LABELS + _PAIRS[: 256 - len(LABELS)]
+DEFAULT_INSTRUCTIONS = {
+    "choice": "Which option applies to the state?",
+    "noul": "Is the statement true, or is the answer to the question yes?",
+    "score": "Which level describes the state?",
+}
+NOUL_DEFAULTS = {
+    "true": "the statement is true / the answer is yes",
+    "false": "the statement is false / the answer is no",
+}
+#: Placed where a suffix goes to find where the shared prefix ends.
+PREFIX_MARK = "QEV_PREFIX_MARK"
+
+
+def render_state(value: Any, strip: bool = False) -> str:
+    """Strings as they are (stripped with ``strip``), others as indented JSON."""
+    if value is None:
+        return ""
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return value.strip() if strip else value
+    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
+
+
+def render_suffix(type_name: str, instructions: Any, criteria: Any) -> str:
+    """The question, its options under slot labels and the answer line."""
+    if type_name == "noul":
+        criteria = criteria or {}
+        names = ["yes", "no"]
+        descriptions = [
+            d if criteria.get(k) is None else criteria[k]
+            for k, d in NOUL_DEFAULTS.items()
+        ]
+    elif type_name == "choice":
+        names, descriptions = list(criteria), list(criteria.values())
+    else:
+        names, descriptions = [f"level {i}" for i in range(len(criteria))], criteria
+    lines = []
+    for label, name, desc in zip(SLOT_LABELS, names, descriptions):
+        text = render_state(desc, strip=True)
+        lines.append(f"{label}. {name}: {text}" if text else f"{label}. {name}")
+    header = "Rate the state:" if type_name == "score" else "Question:"
+    question = render_state(instructions, strip=True) or DEFAULT_INSTRUCTIONS[type_name]
+    kind = "letter" if len(names) <= len(LABELS) else "label"
+    options, labels = "\n".join(lines), ", ".join(SLOT_LABELS[: len(names)])
+    return (
+        f"{header} {question}\n\nOptions:\n{options}\n\n"
+        f"Answer with one {kind}: {labels}."
+    )

+class SlotLMStrategy(NextTokenStrategy):
+    """Slot-readout models: one PrefixLM request per question on ``slot_prompt``."""
+
+    MAX_SCORE_LEVELS = 10

+    MAX_OPTIONS = 255

+    def __init__(self, context: ReadContext):
+        model_config = context.engine_client.model_config
+        if model_config.head_dtype != torch.float32:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "slot reads need the fp32 LM head the checkpoint was trained "
+                f"with, but head_dtype is {model_config.head_dtype}"
+            )
+        super().__init__(context)
+        # read() renders no media, though the base model takes images.
+        self.modalities = frozenset()
+        self.max_model_len = model_config.max_model_len
+        n_slots = model_config.hf_config.modeling_overrides.get(
+            "n_slots", len(slot_prompt.SLOT_LABELS)
+        )
+        # Each slot label's own token must also be the reply's first token.
+        labels = slot_prompt.SLOT_LABELS[:n_slots]
+        _, self.slot_ids = reply_label_ids(
+            self._tokenizer(), self._generation_prompt(), labels
+        )
+        if any(self._tokens(label) != [i] for label, i in zip(labels, self.slot_ids)):
+            raise ValueError("the slot labels' tokens differ at the start of the reply")
+        # read() tokenizes the state once and each suffix on its own, which
+        # needs the suffix to start a pre-token after the prefix.
+        prefix = self._prefix_text("x")
+        for type_name in ("choice", "score"):
+            suffix = slot_prompt.render_suffix(type_name, None, {"x": None})
+            tail = self._prompt("x", suffix)[len(prefix) :]
+            if self._tokens(prefix) + self._tokens(tail) != self._tokens(prefix + tail):
+                raise ValueError("the slot prompt's suffix merges with its prefix")
+
+    def limits(self) -> DecisionLimits:
+        return DecisionLimits(
+            max_questions=64,
+            max_options=min(
+                len(self.slot_ids), self.MAX_OPTIONS, MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS
+            ),
+            labeled=False,
+        )
+
+    def render_state(self, state: Any) -> str:
+        return slot_prompt.render_state(state)
+
+    def _generation_prompt(self) -> list[int]:
+        return self._tokens(self._prompt("x", "y"))
+
+    def _prompt(self, state: str, suffix: str) -> str:
+        prompt = self._tokenizer().apply_chat_template(
+            [
+                {"role": "system", "content": slot_prompt.SYSTEM_PROMPT},
+                {"role": "user", "content": f"<state>\n{state}\n</state>\n\n{suffix}"},
+            ],
+            tokenize=False,
+            add_generation_prompt=True,
+            enable_thinking=False,
+        )
+        assert isinstance(prompt, str)

+
+    def _tokens(self, text: str) -> list[int]:
+        return self._tokenizer().encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
+
+    def _prefix_text(self, state: str) -> str:
+        """The prompt up to where the suffix starts."""
+        marked = self._prompt(state, slot_prompt.PREFIX_MARK)
+        # The last mark is the suffix's: the state may contain the mark too.
+        return marked[: marked.rindex(slot_prompt.PREFIX_MARK)]

+    def _suffix(self, q: Question) -> str:

+                f"{self.MAX_SCORE_LEVELS} levels for this model"

+            criteria = {o.name: o.description for o in q.options}

+            if prefix_len < len(ids):

+        cudagraph_mode: CUDAGraphMode,
+        block_tables: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...],
+        slot_mappings: torch.Tensor,
+        attn_groups: list[list[AttentionGroup]],

+            cudagraph_mode,
+            block_tables,
+            slot_mappings,

+            kv_cache_config,

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Prefix caching for PrefixLM requests, which send their prefix length in
+`extra_args["prefix_lm_len"]`: salts each prefix's blocks by its digest, as the KV
+of every prefix token depends on the whole prefix, caps hits at the prefix and
+prefills the rest of the prompt in one step."""
+
+import copy
+import hashlib
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheBlocks
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.async_scheduler import AsyncScheduler
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler
+from vllm.v1.request import Request
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+PREFIX_LM_LEN = "prefix_lm_len"
+"""`SamplingParams.extra_args` key of the length of a prompt's PrefixLM prefix."""
+
+PREFIX_LM_SALT = "prefix-lm:"
+"""Start of the `cache_salt` of every PrefixLM request, and of no other."""
+
+
+def prefix_lm_len(
+    params: SamplingParams | None, prompt_token_ids: Sequence[int] | None
+) -> int | None:
+    """The valid PrefixLM prefix length a request sends, else None."""
+    extra_args = params.extra_args if params is not None else None
+    prefix_len = extra_args.get(PREFIX_LM_LEN) if extra_args else None
+    if (
+        type(prefix_len) is int
+        and prompt_token_ids is not None
+        and 0 < prefix_len <= len(prompt_token_ids)
+    ):
+        return prefix_len
+    return None
+
+
+def prefix_lm_salt(prefix_token_ids: Sequence[int], cache_salt: str | None) -> str:
+    """PrefixLM `cache_salt`: namespace, prefix digest, then the caller's salt."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(
+        np.asarray(prefix_token_ids, dtype="<i8").tobytes()
+    ).hexdigest()
+    salt = PREFIX_LM_SALT + digest
+    return f"{salt}:{cache_salt}" if cache_salt else salt
+
+
+def _request_prefix_lm_len(request: Request) -> int | None:
+    return prefix_lm_len(request.sampling_params, request.prompt_token_ids)
+
+
+class PrefixLMScheduler(Scheduler):
+    def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
+        # Model hooks pick this class before async scheduling is decided, so
+        # build the async twin here when the engine runs async.
+        vllm_config = kwargs["vllm_config"] if "vllm_config" in kwargs else args[0]
+        if cls is PrefixLMScheduler and vllm_config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling:
+            cls = PrefixLMAsyncScheduler
+        return super().__new__(cls)
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        # Scheduler calls _mamba_block_aligned_split only in this mode.
+        if self.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching and not (
+            self.need_mamba_block_aligned_split
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{type(self).__name__} needs a hybrid model in Mamba 'align' "
+                "cache mode"
+            )
+
+    def add_request(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        params = request.sampling_params
+        if (
+            (request.resumable or request.mm_features)
+            and params is not None
+            and PREFIX_LM_LEN in (params.extra_args or {})
+        ):
+            # Later inputs and encoder budgets can cut such a prompt short.
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Requests with streamed or multimodal inputs ignore %s",
+                PREFIX_LM_LEN,
+            )
+            request.sampling_params = params = copy.copy(params)
+            params.extra_args = dict(params.extra_args or {})
+            del params.extra_args[PREFIX_LM_LEN]
+        # A streaming update re-adds an existing request.
+        if request.request_id not in self.requests:
+            self._salt_by_kind(request)
+        super().add_request(request)
+
+    def _salt_by_kind(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        """Salt PrefixLM requests by prefix; keep causal requests out."""
+        prefix_len = _request_prefix_lm_len(request)
+        salt = request.cache_salt
+        if prefix_len is None:
+            if not (salt and salt.startswith(PREFIX_LM_SALT)):
+                return
+            salt = f"causal:{salt}"
+        else:
+            assert request.prompt_token_ids is not None
+            own = prefix_lm_salt(request.prompt_token_ids[:prefix_len], None)
+            if salt == own or (salt and salt.startswith(f"{own}:")):
+                return
+            salt = f"{own}:{salt}" if salt else own
+        request.cache_salt = salt
+        request.block_hashes.clear()
+        request.update_block_hashes()
+
+    def _get_local_prefix_cache_hit(
+        self, request: Request, max_cache_hit_length: int | None = None
+    ) -> tuple[KVCacheBlocks, int, int, bool]:
+        prefix_len = _request_prefix_lm_len(request)
+        if prefix_len is None:
+            return super()._get_local_prefix_cache_hit(request, max_cache_hit_length)
+        # KV past the prefix depends on the rest of the prompt, and a hit keeps
+        # the last prompt token to compute.
+        cap = min(prefix_len, request.num_tokens - 1)
+        if max_cache_hit_length is not None:
+            cap = min(cap, max_cache_hit_length)
+        return super()._get_local_prefix_cache_hit(request, cap)
+
+    def _mamba_block_aligned_split(
+        self,
+        request: Request,
+        num_new_tokens: int,
+        num_new_local_computed_tokens: int = 0,
+        num_external_computed_tokens: int = 0,
+    ) -> int:
+        start = (
+            request.num_computed_tokens
+            + num_new_local_computed_tokens
+            + num_external_computed_tokens
+        )
+        prefix_lm = (
+            start < request.num_prompt_tokens
+            and _request_prefix_lm_len(request) is not None
+        )
+        if (
+            prefix_lm
+            and start % self.cache_config.block_size == 0
+            and start + num_new_tokens == request.num_tokens
+        ):
+            # A whole prompt from a block boundary needs no Mamba split, which
+            # would stop at a shared-prefix junction.
+            return num_new_tokens
+        num_new_tokens = super()._mamba_block_aligned_split(
+            request,
+            num_new_tokens,
+            num_new_local_computed_tokens,
+            num_external_computed_tokens,
+        )
+        if prefix_lm and start + num_new_tokens < request.num_prompt_tokens:
+            # Zero keeps the request waiting at the head of the queue.
+            return 0
+        return num_new_tokens
+
+

   (streamed requests still drop it), and each media item inside the prefix goes into the prefix salt.
2. **Warn when prefixes can barely be cached.** With a Mamba backend that saves no prefill checkpoints (e.g. the
   Triton/FLA GDN backend on main), a prefix is reused only when its length is a multiple of the Mamba block size.
   The scheduler now says so once.
3. **A PrefixLM prompt no step can prefill.** It returned 0 tokens forever, a silent head-of-line hang. It now
   finishes with a validation error. Only the prompt has to fit a step; outputs of a resumed request don't count.

A generic `prefix_lm_len` request on another model could still wait forever, so a validation error in the scheduler is the right guard.
